Restaurant · Hard

Alert Limit: 6 · Loot: Treasure · For: any session wanting maximum disaster

The Objective

The chef's personal recipe notebook, kept in the back office. A rival baker — a wasp, and nobody is happy about it — hired the crew. The place closes at 11; the crew moves at midnight. Except dinner service ran late.

What the Crew Sees at the Score

A mid-sized restaurant — kitchen, dining room, bar, small office. In plain sight: two closing staff finishing cleanup, and a kitchen that is still warm and smells extraordinary (a spider with Easily Distracted may have it triggered on entry). Two ways in: the alley vent over the bar, or under the kitchen's back door.

Present only what's visible. The intel, the threats, and the unknown obstacle are ST information — let Planning reveal the rest.

The restaurant. A: the alley vent, behind the bar. B: the gap under the back door. H: the two closing staff. R: the rat, under the dishwasher, beside the corridor door. The kitchen floor is freshly mopped (sheen); the steel counters are slippery (glints); the stove is hot. The swinging door and the serving hatch both join the dining room to the kitchen; the corridor door and the pipe gap behind the dishwasher both lead out of it, and both pass the rat. Storyteller's copy: anything dashed in red is the unknown obstacle — keep it off what the crew sees.

One square = one spider. Gold letters are entry points, red tokens are where threats start, numbered circles are the Suggested Obstacles, and E1/E2 lie on the dashed gold escape route.

Intel the crew can uncover by Casing — one true detail per Success, and never more than this list (extra Successes buy nothing; Casing never reveals the unknown obstacle):

  • The staff move unpredictably with no set route.
  • A rat lives under the dishwasher and runs protection for the block — he'll want something.
  • The office door sticks.
  • The snap trap by the back door is new this week; it caught the rat's cousin.
  • The kitchen floor was mopped at closing.

Two closing staff, Alert Humans, starting in the dining room. At the end of each round — outside turn order, each exchange of crew actions (Chapter 9) — roll 1d6 for each: 1–2, the dining room; 3–4, the kitchen; 5, the corridor; 6, a trash run out the back door, which stays propped open until the next 6.

Each round: [[/gmr 1d6]]{Staffer 1} [[/gmr 1d6]]{Staffer 2}

He wants the trap gone, and to be treated like a professional. The crew gets one pitch: Persuasion, opposed by his Haggle 4; offering the trap, food or a favour owed is −1 Difficulty. On a Success, he grants safe passage and stays out of it. On a Partial, the deal holds, but the trap comes first (jamming it is Engineering 3). On a Failure there's no deal: he blocks the way out of the kitchen, and getting past him is a fight. The deal goes bad the moment there's a fight, or if the crew leaves with the trap still set: the Alert rises by 2, once, and he fights (Brawl 4).

ST information. Don't foreshadow it in the Score — let it arrive.

A third staff member fell asleep in the break room. They wake the first time the crew makes noise within 4 squares of the break room — any Partial or Failure there, a sneeze, the sticking office door — or when the Alert reaches 5 (Chapter 15: they stir). Awake, they're an Alert Human, and they head straight for the office: their phone is on the desk.

Obstacles 1–4 are the heist: each takes two successful rolls (Partial or better), and a group check counts as both. E1 and E2 are the suggested Escape obstacles: one successful roll each, and at least one of them never needs Athletics. Difficulties are for a calm location; the Alert raises them. Opposed means the creature rolls first, and its Successes + 1 are your Difficulty.

#ObstacleRoll (Difficulty)
1The dining room — two staff moving unpredictably, no patrol pattern. They are Alert Humans (Deception or Stealth 4).Stealth or Deception (4); the tables are cover (Chapter 3)
2The kitchen — warm, incredible smells. Easily Distracted triggers. And the floor has just been mopped.Cross unseen: Stealth (2), the dishwasher's hum covers you — (4) if a staffer's in here · the wet floor: double movement, or Acrobatics (2)
3The rat. Negotiations. He wants something. Work out what.His deal: Persuasion, opposed (Haggle 4) · no deal: Brawl, opposed (his Brawl 4), and it's gone bad
4(Unknown) The office door sticks, and the staffer asleep next door wakes at the first noise nearby, or at Alert 5 — and comes for their phone.The notebook won't fit under the door. Ease it: Engineering (3) · shove it: Athletics (3), and it scrapes: +1 Alert · once they're up: Stealth or Deception (4)
E1Back up the corridor with the notebook, the staff still on the move.Stealth or Deception (4)
E2The back door. The notebook won't fit under it, so get it open — or wait for a trash run to prop it. And the trap, if the crew still owes the rat.Work the handle with a silk line: Engineering (3) · hang on it together: Athletics (3) · jam the trap: Engineering (3)
